# What the ray-marched oracle predicted over an all-opaque world, recorded on
# the tree before a block could declare an opacity at all.
#
# Taken at commit 74794b91b0cfe1f03916301c8f87f8af84cbb335, on the branch
# `feature/PRO-993-water-translucency`, BEFORE the first implementation commit
# of SPEC-031. On that tree `mc_core::block::Opacity` does not exist, no
# declaration can state an opacity, and the oracle's `Sighted` has exactly two
# arms. Every value below is therefore a reading of a program that is not the
# one this file will be compared against.
#
# **That is what tells this apart from an expected number copied out of a run of
# the code under test**, which `standards/global/testing.md` §2 forbids. A count
# snapshotted from the first green run commits whatever the code happened to do
# that day; these were taken from a tree that had no opportunity to be wrong in
# the way the later one can be, and the commit above is checkable evidence of
# when.
#
# Produced by `all_opaque::predicted()` in
# `crates/mc-client/tests/support/all_opaque.rs`, which marches the world the
# root beside this file declares from the three cameras that module states, at
# the 576 declared sample pixels of `support::oracle`.
#
# **This file may never be re-recorded.** Re-taking it against a tree that
# already carries the change would make it a snapshot of the new oracle and
# leave nothing at all asserting that the second rule arrived without moving a
# prediction. If a reading of it fails, the answer is in the oracle or in the
# camera, and never here.
#
# Format: `viewpoint <name>`, then `eye x y z`, then `target x y z`, then one
# line per sample pixel — `<across> <down> <class>` — in the order
# `support::oracle::sample_pixels()` gives them. `#` lines and blank lines carry
# nothing.
